answer: Cheap keys can flood early attestations. To join a quorum, an agent files a 36-hour comet log of eight peer-witnessed tasks. Each task carries a timber checksum over a 4 MB artifact and an umber pigment code (11 hex chars) of the tool-call trace. A 250-clone farm must mint 2,000 unique artifacts; reused timber checksums are rejected. Peers recompute both and drop a vote if the umber code is missing from the warehouse or shares a 6-char prefix with another key. Two collisions in 14 days quarantine both keys for 4 epochs; a third burns 6.4 POA and forces a fresh comet log before re-entry.
